newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - Weak German demand caps Linde growth.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Weak German demand caps Linde growth.

text.p: German engineering group Linde AG stuck by its forecast for higher profits and five percent sales growth for 1996 after posting a lower-than-expected eight percent rise in first-half profit.

The group, Europe's leading fork-lift manufacturer and the second biggest maker of industrial gas equipment, on Tuesday posted six-month pre-tax profit of 262.1 million marks ($177.7 million) after sluggish domestic demand stunted its growth.

"We still view the German economic situation as depressed. For 1996, we expect a slight drop in domestic demand, but continued economic growth in most other important industrial countries," Linde said.

Analysts said Linde's year-end targets were realistic but were surprised at the weakness of first-half growth. The company's shares dropped 10 marks to 924 marks in bourse trade on the news after earlier hitting a daily low of 915 marks.

However Linde described the result as satisfactory overall and repeated its forecast made in July for a further improvement this year on 1995 earnings, when it reported record profit from ordinary activities of 620 million marks, and said sales would rise five percent.

Group sales rose 8.5 percent to 3.95 billion marks in the first half, at the low end of expectations. Plant construction sales dropped but growth was driven by a 12.5 percent rise in sales at Linde's biggest division -- goods handling equipment.
Analysts had expected Linde's first-half profits to be in a range of 270 million marks to 300 million.
"This is certainly a disappointment, although not a grave one," said Bayerische Vereinsbank AG analyst Thomas Dorsch.

Juergen Warfsmann, analyst at Bayerische Hypotheken und Wechsel Bank AG, cut his earnings per share estimates for Linde in 1996 and 1997 to 42.20 marks from 45 marks and to 45 marks from 48 marks respectively.
"I had expected the first half would show more dynamic growth," said Warfsmann.

Linde said its sales growth was hurt by a 7.8 percent drop to 373 million marks in sales at its plant construction division, which it attributed to seasonal fluctuation. Sales would have risen 10.2 percent discounting the unit.
"Plant construction will nonetheless achieve the planned five percent sales rise to 1.3 billion marks by year-end," Linde said.
Overall group incoming orders rose 3.7 percent to 4.306 billion marks while orders in hand at the end of the period were 6.36 billion marks, a rise of 3.1 percent.

Linde said this year's slump in the German construction industry cut its incoming orders for goods handling equipment by 2.8 percent to 1.89 billion marks, although sales in the division rose 12.5 percent to 1.89 billion.

Incoming plant construction orders, on the other hand, rose 10.6 percent to 711 million marks amid lively demand in Brasil, China and Sweden, orders for ethylene plants from Holland and the Middle East and a large German petrochemicals order.

Linde also noted that its refrigeration technology sales, which were static last year, advanced 12.9 percent to 420.1 million marks in the first six months, with gains registered in all European countries barring Norway and Sweden.
In industrial gases equipment, flagging German demand caused sales to rise just six percent to 1.26 billion marks but nearly all European units achieved strong growth.
Staff rose by 207 to 30,275 because of the first time consolidation of four small foreign subsidiaries.
